key_insight: Computer-vision-informed void nucleation makes shock damage predictions sensitive to microstructure, with representative microstructures needed to reproduce measured free-surface velocity.
engineering_relevance: The model supports microstructure-aware prediction of spallation in shock-loaded tantalum while selectively resolving microstructure to limit computational cost.
method: Predict a void-nucleation susceptibility field from grain orientations and grain-boundary energy using computer vision.
Combine susceptibility with a local maximum-principal-stress barrier in a continuum damage model.
Couple damage to crystal plasticity within a Lagrangian shock simulation.
evidence_signal: Calibrated at a flyer velocity of 196 m/s, the model matched major experimental free-surface-velocity features and reproduced a 214 m/s case without further parameter changes.
watch_item: Predictions depend on representative microstructure inputs, and deviations remain in late-time ringing.
paper_title: A mesoscale damage model for void nucleation and growth in shock loaded microstructure informed by computer vision
